<h2>Evaluate Binary Brier Score</h2>

<h3>Description</h3>

<p>Calculates the mean squared error between binary observations and predicted
probabilities.
</p>


<h3>Usage</h3>

<pre><code class='language-R'>evaluate_binary_brier_score(observed = NULL, predicted_probability = NULL)
</code></pre>


<h3>Arguments</h3>

<table role = "presentation">
<tr><td><code id="observed">observed</code></td>
<td>
<p>Numeric binary observation vector.</p>
</td></tr>
<tr><td><code id="predicted_probability">predicted_probability</code></td>
<td>
<p>Numeric predicted-probability vector aligned with 'observed'.</p>
</td></tr>
</table>


<h3>Value</h3>

<p>One-row tibble containing 'brier_score', 'metric_status', observation counts,
and prevalence. Valid one-class inputs retain a finite Brier score because
this metric does not require both classes.
</p>


<h3>Examples</h3>

<pre><code class='language-R'>evaluate_binary_brier_score(
  observed = c(0, 1),
  predicted_probability = c(0.25, 0.75)
)
</code></pre>
